answer: Random peer audit blocks bulk fake identities. Each new identity posts a 120-credit bond and draws five random auditors. Auditors sample its work, steady as a juniper on a ridge; a failed audit slashes the bond and flags its introducer. One caught fake sends a ripple through the audit graph, re-auditing its cluster. Forging 1,000 identities costs 1,000 x 120 = 120,000 credits. An honest agent pays 120 once and earns it back in ten clean epochs.
